```{r}
# Load your dataset 
data(obesity.levels)

# Inspect variable types and summary stats
summary(obesity.levels)
str(obesity.levels)
```


```{r}
numeric_vars <- obesity.levels %>% select(where(is.numeric))
summary_stats <- numeric_vars %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), list(mean = mean, sd = sd)))
print(summary_stats)

```

```{r}
# Select variables for analysis (choose continuous/numeric ones for correlation)
analysis_vars <- c("Age", "Height", "Weight", "FCVC", "NCP", "CH2O", "FAF", "TUE")
obesity_sub <- obesity.levels[, analysis_vars]
```


```{r}
# Means and SDs
desc_stats <- data.frame(
  Mean = sapply(obesity_sub, mean),
  SD = sapply(obesity_sub, sd)
)
desc_stats
# Correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(obesity_sub)
cor_matrix
```



```{r}
# Make missingness depend on observed variable (e.g., Age)
obesity_mar <- obesity_sub
for (var in analysis_vars[-1]) { # Exclude Age
  missing_prob <- plogis(scale(obesity_sub$Age)) # Logistic function
  obesity_mar[runif(nrow(obesity_sub)) < missing_prob*0.3, var] <- NA # Adjust 0.3 to get ~20% missing
}
```


```{r}
# Make missingness depend on unobserved values (e.g., high Weight values more likely missing)
obesity_mnar <- obesity_sub
for (var in analysis_vars) {
  missing_prob <- plogis(scale(obesity_sub[[var]])) # Missingness depends on its own value
  obesity_mnar[runif(nrow(obesity_sub)) < missing_prob*0.3, var] <- NA
}
```







```{r}
### 2. MAR Mechanism (Missing At Random) ###
set.seed(123)
obesity_mar <- obesity_full

# Continuous variables: Missingness depends on observed 'Age'
for(var in cont_vars) {
  if(var != "Age") {
    missing_prob <- pnorm(scale(obesity_full$Age)) # Normal CDF
    missing_indices <- which(runif(nrow(obesity_full)) < missing_prob*0.35)
    obesity_mar[missing_indices, var] <- NA
  }
}

# Categorical variables: Missingness depends on observed 'Gender'
for(var in cat_vars) {
  missing_prob <- ifelse(obesity_full$Gender == "Male", 0.3, 0.1)
  missing_indices <- which(runif(nrow(obesity_full)) < missing_prob)
  obesity_mar[missing_indices, var] <- NA
}

# Visualize
marginplot(obesity_mar[, c("Weight", "Age")], col = c("blue", "red", "orange"))
```


```{r}
### 3. MNAR Mechanism (Missing Not At Random) ###
set.seed(123)
obesity_mnar <- obesity_full

# Continuous variables: Missingness depends on their own values
for(var in cont_vars) {
  missing_prob <- plogis(2*scale(obesity_full[[var]])) # Logistic function
  missing_indices <- which(runif(nrow(obesity_full)) < missing_prob*0.3)
  obesity_mnar[missing_indices, var] <- NA
}

# Categorical variables: Missingness depends on unobserved target
for(var in cat_vars) {
  missing_prob <- plogis(0.5*as.numeric(scale(as.numeric(obesity_full$NObeyesdad))))
  missing_indices <- which(runif(nrow(obesity_full)) < missing_prob)
  obesity_mnar[missing_indices, var] <- NA
}

# For binary vars: Higher probability of missing for one category
obesity_mnar$FAVC[obesity_full$FAVC == "yes" & 
                  runif(nrow(obesity_full)) < 0.4] <- NA

# Visualize MNAR pattern
ggplot(obesity_full, aes(x = NObeyesdad, y = Weight)) +
  geom_point(data = obesity_mnar[!is.na(obesity_mnar$Weight),], color = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = obesity_mnar[is.na(obesity_mnar$Weight),], 
             aes(y = mean(Weight, na.rm = TRUE)), color = "red", alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "MNAR Pattern: Missing Weight vs Obesity Level")
```


```{r}
### Save all datasets ###
missing_data_sets <- list(
  original = original_data,
  MCAR = obesity_mcar,
  MAR = obesity_mar,
  MNAR = obesity_mnar
)

### Verification of Missingness Patterns ###

# Function to check missing percentages
check_missingness <- function(data) {
  sapply(data, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
}

# Print missing percentages
lapply(missing_data_sets[-1], check_missingness)

# Statistical test for MAR mechanism
# Should show association between missingness and observed variables
lm_missing_weight <- glm(is.na(Weight) ~ Age + Gender, 
                        data = obesity_mar, family = binomial)
summary(lm_missing_weight)

# Statistical test for MNAR mechanism
# Should show association between missingness and (when available) its own value
if(any(!is.na(obesity_mnar$Weight))) {
  wilcox.test(Weight ~ is.na(Weight), data = obesity_full)
}
```
